11.text: These marital ties with strangers lead us to the so-called “prostitution

12.text: of hospitality.” It cannot be positively ascertained whether in ancient times

13.text: that custom existed among the Chukchee. According to Russian accounts of

14.text: ancient times, it was customary for Russian merchants at the spring Chukchee

15.text: fairs to visit the rich maritime traders. They would bring with them iron,

16.text: kettles, tobacco in bags, and gave all this to the host as a present. The

17.text: host, in return, offered his wife to the guest, having first covered the sleeping-

18.text: place with beaver, fox, and marten furs, numerous enough to cover the value

19.text: of the present. Nowadays no such custom exists.

20.text: As indicated above, Chukchee girls and women are noted for their loose

21.text: conduct, and willingly comply with the wishes of Russian guests and acquaint-

22.text: ances for an insignificant remuneration. The Chukchee, however, class even

23.text: such cases under the head of group-marriage. In regard to these matters,

24.text: very humorous misunderstandings occur between the Russians and the Chuk-

25.text: chee. Thus, on one of his journeys through the Kolyma district, the chief

26.text: officer Karzin obviously had intimate intercourse with one of the wives or

27.text: relatives of a rich reindeer-breeder, Omrêlqoˊt. When Karzin returned to

28.text: Sredne-Kolymsk, the following incident occurred. Karzin’s housekeeper (he
